correctness.rationale: Exact exponential Laplace transform and rational quotient derivative give midpoint sign B(q,lambda); monotonicity in lambda proves one boundary. C(q,lambda)>0 by its negative discriminant for q>1 verifies quartic degeneracy. Evenness, continuity and decay prove noncentral global existence below threshold; no uniqueness or global optimality above threshold is inferred. Checker verifies 698 finite identities and regimes but is not used as an infinite proof.

The shared-frailty joint probability is a three-denominator rational function with a different critical root; a product-of-two-Cauchy theorem does not imply it.

value.rationale: Correlated variation in propagule pressure is ecologically motivated and changes joint success probabilities; the sharp stability threshold and strict earlier stabilization relative to independent environments identify a structural, quantitative effect that marginal establishment curves alone conceal. The result is limited to one-dimensional sites and local stability, with global noncentral existence only below threshold.
